name: Reese McIntosh Rowling
profile: Geologist and Corpus Christi oilman (born 1928, Waycross, Georgia) who co-founded Tana Oil and Gas in 1972, later sold to Texaco; father of Robert Rowling (TRT Holdings). Died in 2001.
notes: Deceased (2001) per Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese_Rowling . Family wealth now associated with son Robert Rowling / TRT Holdings.

name: Patrick Bowlen
profile: Longtime owner of the NFL's Denver Broncos (from 1984), winning three Super Bowls. Died June 13, 2019, aged 75; team later sold to the Walton-Penner group in 2022.

name: Paul Salteri
current_role: Founder and Chairman, CAGES Foundation (Salteri family private ancillary fund); former Chairman, Tenix Group
profile: Eldest son of Transfield co-founder Carlo Salteri. Became joint MD of Transfield in 1989; after the 1995 family split he ran the Salteri side as Tenix (MD 1997-2007, then chairman), selling Tenix Defence to BAE Systems in 2008 and the remaining Tenix assets to Downer EDI in 2014. Now focused on philanthropy via the CAGES Foundation.
interesting_fact: Transfield, the company his father co-founded, won a A$6bn contract in 1989 to build ten Anzac-class frigates for Australia and New Zealand, becoming Australia's largest defence company; that business became Tenix Defence.
deep_cut_fact: With his wife Sandra he set up CAGES Foundation to support First Nations early-childhood services; after asking Indigenous communities why investment often fails ('because they don't trust us'), the foundation shifted to trust-based, less onerous grant-making.
notes: Low public profile; best route is CAGES Foundation (Sydney). Trained as an accountant (UNSW BCom 1971), joined Transfield 1978. Tenix itself no longer exists as an operating group.

name: Ellis Short
current_role: Founder, Kildare Partners (distressed European real estate private equity)
profile: American financier (b. 1960, Independence, Missouri) who became president of Dallas private equity firm Lone Star Funds and ran its Asian operations, then founded Kildare Partners in 2013 to buy distressed European property and non-performing loans. Owned Sunderland AFC 2008-2018.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he paid about GBP 23m for Skibo Castle in Scotland, the members-only club famous for hosting Madonna and Guy Ritchie's 2000 wedding.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he was an engineer: he earned a mechanical engineering degree from Missouri University of Science and Technology (then Missouri-Rolla) in 1983 and started his career at General Electric.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Only route found is Kildare Partners (offices in Dallas/Westlake TX, London, Dublin, Bermuda). Returned to the US from London in 2017.

name: Peter Green
profile: Manchester-born investor who married into the Mitchell family (Luscar coal, Alberta) and led the family business; family later held stakes in the Maybourne hotel group and bought Bermuda's Hamilton Princess in 2012. Died in Bermuda on 7 November 2024, aged 89.
notes: Deceased 7 Nov 2024 per Bermuda Government condolence https://www.gov.bm/news/premier-burt-peter-green-condolence and Royal Gazette https://royalgazette.com/general/news/article/20241114/bng-remembers-peter-green . Family interests (Hamilton Princess, Sugar Beach St Lucia) now associated with sons; identity matched via 'mining and inheritance' (Luscar) source of wealth.

name: Peng Yongdong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, KE Holdings (Beike), NYSE: BEKE / HKEX: 2423
profile: Stanley Peng Yongdong co-founded KE Holdings (Beike), China's largest housing transaction and services platform, which grew out of the Lianjia brokerage; he has been CEO since its 2018 relaunch and chairman after founder Zuo Hui's death in 2021. Holds an electrical engineering degree from Zhejiang University and an IMBA from Tsinghua.
interesting_fact: KE operates Lianjia, one of the world's largest real estate brokerages, and has expanded into home rentals and renovation.
deep_cut_fact: Before real estate he was a senior consultant at IBM (2006-2010), joining Lianjia from management consulting.
notes: A March 2025 trade report claimed he resigned as chairman, but KE's later 2025/2026 results releases still list him as Chairman and CEO. Route via KE investor relations.

name: Tang Ye
current_role: Chairman (since 2007) and CEO, Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology (SSE STAR: 688188)
profile: Tang Ye co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology in September 2007 in Shanghai's Zizhu high-tech zone, near Shanghai Jiao Tong University, where he earned a master's in engineering management. The company makes control systems and software for fiber laser cutting machines and listed on the STAR Market in August 2019; he remains its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Friendess was one of China's first private companies developing fiber laser cutting control systems and now supplies control systems to more than 400 laser equipment makers.
notes: Low international profile; communicates in Chinese. Investor posts relaying a SJTU video interview say the five co-founders took tiny salaries early on and never raised outside capital, but this is unverified so it is not used as a fact.

name: Kuan Kam Hon
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hartalega Holdings Bhd (Malaysia)
profile: High-school dropout who started in his father's KL home-building firm in 1969, founded label maker Timol Weaving in 1978, then pivoted into medical gloves in 1988 as Hartalega, now one of the world's largest nitrile glove makers. He acts as mentor and spokesman, leaving operations to his sons.
interesting_fact: In 2005 Hartalega launched the world's first lightweight nitrile glove (4.7g vs an industry norm of 6g+), a product most rivals doubted could work.
deep_cut_fact: The name Hartalega combines two Malay words meaning 'relief assets'; he converted his struggling woven-label and badge plant into a latex glove factory as demand rose in the early AIDS-epidemic years.
notes: Also known as Kwan Kam Onn; wealth shared with brother Kuan Kam Peng. Glove sector is cyclical; avoid wealth-decline framing. Route via Hartalega corporate/IR (Sepang, Selangor); no published IR email verified.

name: Li Guiru
profile: Listed on Hurun China lists 2017-2023 (with Liu Aisen) with wealth attributed to 'Center International' (software & services). Could not identify the underlying company or confirm her role from public sources.
notes: Identity not confirmed: searches in English and Chinese (李桂茹, 刘爱森, 中心国际) found nothing. Lane's web-search budget ran out before further attempts; worth a re-check against the Hurun China list entry to find the company's Chinese name.

name: Louis Bacon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and principal investment manager, Moore Capital Management; Founder and Chairman, The Moore Charitable Foundation
profile: North Carolina-born macro trader who profited in the 1987 crash and founded Moore Capital in 1989, becoming one of Wall Street's best-known macro managers. He returned outside capital in 2019 and now runs Moore mainly as a family/employee investment firm, while focusing heavily on land, water and wildlife conservation through the Moore Charitable Foundation (founded 1992).
interesting_fact: He named Moore Capital after his own middle name, and launched Moore Global Investments in 1990 with $25,000 inherited from his family.
deep_cut_fact: His Wall Street start came from a summer job: while working on a fishing boat on Long Island he met NYSE specialist Walter Frank, who gave him a clerking job at Walter N. Frank & Co. during his college summers. He later ran a floor 'runner' job at the New York Cotton Exchange.
notes: Energy angle: has written publicly against Drax biomass sourcing (Daily Mail op-ed linked from louisbacon.com) and on wildfire/forest health and offshore drilling. Ann Colley, Moore Capital's Director of Public Relations and Charitable Giving and Foundation Executive Director, is the published PR lead (https://www.moorecharitable.org/leadership/ann-colley/).

name: Jeffrey S. Raikes
current_role: Co-founder, Raikes Foundation; board member (Costco, Hudl); former CEO, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
profile: Nebraska farm-raised Stanford engineer who joined Microsoft in 1981, drove Office's product strategy and rose to president of the Microsoft Business Division before retiring in 2008. He then ran the Gates Foundation as CEO (2008-2014) and now co-leads the Seattle-based Raikes Foundation with his wife, focused on youth, education and impact-driven philanthropy.
interesting_fact: In 1992 he joined the local investor group that bought the Seattle Mariners to keep the team from leaving the Pacific Northwest.
deep_cut_fact: Before Microsoft he was Apple's VisiCalc engineering manager in 1980; after 15 months Steve Ballmer recruited him to Microsoft as a product manager. He first learned to program in Pascal on a DEC System 20 at Stanford, where he had prepared for a career in USDA agricultural policy.
notes: Name in input is 'S. Raikes Jeffrey' = Jeffrey S. Raikes. Also namesake of the Jeffrey S. Raikes School of Computer Science and Management at University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Best route: Raikes Foundation press inbox.

name: William Fung
current_role: Deputy Group Chairman, Fung Group (Li & Fung parent), Hong Kong
profile: William Fung Kwok-lun (b. 1949), grandson of Li & Fung co-founder Fung Pak-liu, helped build Li & Fung with brother Victor into the world's biggest consumer-goods sourcing middleman, expanding it across Taiwan, Korea, Singapore and China. He stepped down as Li & Fung chairman in 2020 when it was taken private; the brothers sold LF Logistics to Maersk for $3.4bn in 2022. He remains Deputy Group Chairman of the Fung Group.
interesting_fact: Li & Fung was founded in Guangzhou in 1906 by his grandfather Fung Pak-liu and partner Li To-ming, exporting porcelain and silk.
deep_cut_fact: He studied electrical engineering at Princeton (class of 1970), later endowed the 'Fung Scholarship' there and was named a Princeton trustee in 2009; he also earned an HBS MBA in 1972.
notes: Fung Group also runs the Victor & William Fung Foundation (listed on the leadership page), another possible route. Has served on boards incl. HSBC, CLP, VTech and Singapore Airlines (historical).

name: Sebastian Siemiatkowski
profile: Swedish son of Polish immigrants who co-founded Klarna in 2005 at 23 after selling accounts-receivable services and seeing how painful e-commerce payments were for small merchants. Klarna pioneered buy-now-pay-later, became a licensed European bank and listed on the NYSE in September 2025, the year's largest NYSE IPO. He is a prominent voice on AI replacing corporate headcount.
interesting_fact: He met one of his Klarna co-founders while the two were flipping burgers at a Burger King in Sweden.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Sweden's late-1990s policy of subsidising home-computer ownership for his career, since it let his family buy their first computer; his early business heroes were Richard Branson and IKEA founder Ingvar Kamprad.
notes: Very active publicly on X (widely cited as @klarnaseb) and LinkedIn, posting about AI and Klarna; could not verify the handle from an official page here. Good podcast fit for AI/compute-demand angle (Klarna's 'AI can do all the jobs' stance).

name: Matthew Calkins
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, CEO and President, Appian Corp (Nasdaq: APPN)
profile: Dartmouth economics grad (1994) who worked at MicroStrategy before co-founding Appian in 1999 at age 26, early on building an intranet portal for the US Army. Appian sells low-code process automation and AI software to governments and large enterprises, went public in May 2017, and Calkins still owns a large stake and runs the company from the Washington, DC area.
interesting_fact: He is a champion competitive board gamer with multiple World Boardgaming Championships wins and designs games himself, including Sekigahara, Tin Goose, Charioteer and Magnet.
deep_cut_fact: His abstract game Magnet was runner-up for Games Magazine's Abstract Game of the Year in 2010; at Dartmouth he wrote a game-theory thesis on when a losing hockey team should pull its goalie.

public_contacts.value: cindy.cheng@appian.com (Sr. Director, Global Marketing Communications, listed as media contact)

notes: Accessible, opinionated public speaker on AI (frequent keynotes, writes on 'dimensions of AI'); good podcast candidate. Hockey-thesis fact is from the Forbes profile facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/matthew-calkins/).

name: Paul Marshall
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Marshall Wace; owner of The Spectator and UnHerd, co-owner of GB News
profile: Sir Paul Marshall (b. 1959) worked at Mercury Asset Management before co-founding Marshall Wace with Ian Wace in 1997, now one of the world's largest equity long/short managers with $50bn+ AUM. He has become a major UK media owner (UnHerd, GB News, The Spectator from 2024) and philanthropist, topping the 2024 Sunday Times Giving List.
interesting_fact: Marshall Wace launched in 1997 as one of London's first hedge funds with $50m, half of it from George Soros.
deep_cut_fact: In 1985 he was a research assistant to future Lib Dem leader Charles Kennedy, stood for Parliament in Fulham for the SDP-Liberal Alliance in 1987, and in 2004 co-edited the influential 'Orange Book' with David Laws. He gave GBP 50m to the LSE for the Marshall Institute.

public_contacts.value: George Trefgarne, Boscobel & Partners (Marshall Wace media enquiries), +44 203 642 1310

notes: High-profile, politically engaged media owner; expect PR gatekeeping via Boscobel. Knighted in 2016 'for services to Education and Philanthropy'; was lead non-executive director at the Department for Education 2013-2016.

name: Du Ying (Samantha Du)
current_role: Founder, Chairperson and CEO, Zai Lab (Nasdaq: ZLAB; HKEX: 9688)
profile: Samantha Du (Du Ying), Ph.D., founded Shanghai-based biopharma Zai Lab in 2014 after earlier roles in pharma R&D and healthcare venture investing (including Sequoia Capital China). Zai Lab in-licenses and develops oncology, immunology and neuroscience drugs for China and globally, and listed on Nasdaq in 2017 and in Hong Kong in 2020.
notes: Only her title was verified from Zai Lab's leadership page this session; background details (Sequoia China, listing dates) are from general knowledge and should be double-checked. Web-search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact or IR email was sourced; Zai Lab press releases normally list IR/media contacts.

name: G Ravindra Rao (G. Ravender Rao)
current_role: Chairman, Yashoda Hospitals / Yashoda Healthcare Services, Hyderabad
profile: Engineer by training who started in government service, then built manufacturing businesses before co-founding Hyderabad's Yashoda Hospitals with his brothers Dr G. Surender Rao (MD) and G. Devender Rao. Yashoda grew from a 1989 clinic into a multi-hospital group in Hyderabad (Secunderabad, Somajiguda, Malakpet, Hitec City) with about 4,000 beds; he chairs the group.
interesting_fact: Yashoda performed the first lung transplant in the Telugu states (2012) and the first combined heart-lung transplant there (2017).
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare, in 1978 he founded Yashoda Vacuum Industries, which pioneered manufacturing 'Yashoda Xerox drums', and later set up a metals company supplying a national atomic research centre and defence manufacturers. He grew up in a village in Nalgonda district.
notes: Official spelling is 'G. Ravender Rao'. Hospital's investor-relations director (per leadership page) is a family member, so route via corporate contact form rather than individuals. Says he gives over 10% of earnings to social causes via Yashoda Foundation.

name: Deepak Chimanlal Mehta
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Deepak Nitrite Ltd (Vadodara, India)
profile: Son of Deepak Nitrite founder Chimanlal Khimchand Mehta, a Gujarat chemical trader who incorporated the company in 1970. Deepak Mehta has built it from a sodium nitrite maker into a diversified chemicals group, notably via subsidiary Deepak Phenolics, which makes phenol and acetone at Dahej, Gujarat; his son Maulik Mehta is CEO.
interesting_fact: Deepak Nitrite's 1971 IPO was oversubscribed 20 times, and its first sodium nitrite/nitrate plant at Nadesari, Vadodara started production in 1972.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he took the company into large-scale petrochemical intermediates by promoting Deepak Phenolics, building a phenol and acetone plant at Dahej, Gujarat that also makes pharmaceutical-grade isopropyl alcohol.
notes: Company site was unreachable (503) during research, so no IR/press email verified; Deepak Nitrite's stock-exchange filings list the company secretary/investor contact. Web-search budget ran out before a more personal deep-cut could be found.
